invariants.scope: every admission (decision 2026-10-18 15:23Z): supplied-epoch-binder-check is on surface_kinds.all
invariants.statement: For admission, hb_epoch is observed state: the SV_CHANGE's hb_epoch is the epoch recorded on the org-ledger head receipt its base (base_ref.ledger_head) is bound to ($.hb_reference.epoch of the sealed stegverse.organization-transition-receipt/v1 named by HEAD.json at that commit), as read and sealed by Lane C's base-state readback (Labs#3266 @641f4b03, readback blob fbd453e5, stegverse.sv-change-base-state-readback/v1: hb_epoch slot + hb_epoch_source, sealed by result_sha256). The shared supplied-epoch rule (726248a5) still applies to the read value. Nothing reads a clock and nothing mints an epoch.

supplied_epoch_rule.note: 726248a5 is the sha256 of the function's source segment, not a git object id
supplied_epoch_rule.precedence: UNKNOWN precedence (contract invariant, orchestrator 2026-10-18T15:59Z, narrowed 16:03Z): before 726248a5 is applied, a supplied hb_epoch that is the epoch source (an SV_CHANGE record's hb_epoch; an absent field reads as null) and is JSON null, "", "null" or the literal UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED is FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED (UNKNOWN is FAIL_CLOSED, never DENY). An optional cross-check that is left out (sv_work_items.HB_EPOCH_NOT_CROSS_CHECKED) is not a failure: the sealed epoch stands. Here the verifier deliberately diverges from kernel.py::supplied_epoch_failure, which alone would return HB_EPOCH_NOT_SUPPLIED for null and HB_EPOCH_INVALID (malformed, DENY here) for "", "null" and the sentinel. The pin is unchanged: it still describes the rule applied to every other supplied value and to the sealed slot.

examples.'01024' vs sealed 1024: ALLOW (726248a5 accepts leading zeros; equal by integer value)
examples.'UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED': FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED (precedes 726248a5, which alone would say HB_EPOCH_INVALID)
examples.null / absent record field: FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED (precedes 726248a5, which alone would say HB_EPOCH_NOT_SUPPLIED)
examples.optional cross-check left out: ALLOW on the sealed epoch (cross_checked false)

supplied_epoch_ruling.order: (1) the sealed source: unobserved -> FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED whatever the supplied value; (2) no cross-check supplied (HB_EPOCH_NOT_CROSS_CHECKED) -> ALLOW on the sealed epoch; (3) null/""/"null"/sentinel -> FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED (before the kernel rule); (4) 726248a5 on the supplied value, then integer equality -> DENY HB_EPOCH_MISMATCH
supplied_epoch_ruling.parity: SV-LLM/.github#46 sandbox/s1_supplied_epoch_binder.py::binder_check @64b90721 agrees on every malformed and mismatched value; it predates the UNKNOWN precedence (null/''/'null'/sentinel are DENY there): open alignment item for Lane B
supplied_epoch_ruling.ruling: orchestrator standard 2026-10-18 (both verifiers agree on 60 cases), refined by contract invariant 2026-10-18T15:59Z and narrowed 16:03Z
supplied_epoch_ruling.statement: anything not observed is UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED, which is FAIL_CLOSED, never DENY. Where the supplied value is the epoch source (an SV_CHANGE record's hb_epoch), absent (read as null), JSON null, "", "null" or the literal UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED is FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED; an optional cross-check left out (HB_EPOCH_NOT_CROSS_CHECKED) is not a failure and proceeds on the sealed epoch; any other supplied value that fails 726248a5 (non-digits, below 32, a bool, an int rather than ASCII text, coerced such as '+33') is DENY HB_EPOCH_MISMATCH, and so is a well-formed value that differs from the sealed epoch; the sealed-source-unobserved cases (readback absent, unsealed, neither ALLOW nor DENY HB_EPOCH_MISMATCH, other head, no hb_epoch_source or receipt path, or a clock-derived, non-int or otherwise invalid readback epoch) stay FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED

invariants.statement: A NATIVE record's hb_epoch (ASCII digits) equals, by integer value, $.hb_reference.epoch of the stegverse.organization-transition-receipt/v1 at its base ledger head (SV_CHANGE base_ref.ledger_head, SV_ISSUE observed_base.ledger_head), read from refs/stegverse/organization-ledger: HEAD.json at that commit -> receipts/<receipt_sha256 hex>.json, seal verified (receipt_sha256 = sha256 of the canonical body without it). The epoch is an int >= 32 (not bool, no coercion from other types) from a reference not derived from a clock (kernel.hb_reference, org-kernel/kernel.py:68-74); there is no top-level hb_epoch on the org receipt. Never read from a clock.

It carries no `evidence`; it carries boundary_evidence {operation, profile_id, disposition, communication_id} and repo_receipt_sha256 (verify_source, :627-651). The org ledger retains that sealed stegverse.repo-transition-receipt/v1 beside it at source-receipts/<hex>.json in the same commit (ledger_store.source_key, ledger_store.py:59-61; :1064-1066; organization_ledger_readback.py:89-91). The check receipt is the repo receipt's $.evidence (.stegverse/transition-ledger/emit.py:116), placed there by Lane D's sv_check_receipt append operation and self-identified by $.evidence.schema == stegverse.sv_check_receipt.v1 or $.evidence.kind == 'sv_check_receipt' (then the object minus kind must be the pinned receipt shape). boundary_evidence.operation, when present, must be 'sv_check_receipt'.

invariants.statement: A check-derived SV_ISSUE is a deterministic derivation from the org-ledger-appended non-ALLOW check receipt: source_receipt_ref = that ledger ref (@ its receipt_sha256), failed_predicate = the receipt's failed check, surface = the check's command surface, owning_goal = the required-checks row's owning_goal. Its issue_id does not depend on who runs the derivation, so no lane owns minting: sv_work_items.derive_issue_from_check_receipt is the sanctioned derivation and fixing lanes cite the issue in resolves.
